newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia general orders troops to control roads.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia general orders troops to control roads.

text.p: Cambodia's chief of general staff ordered forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen to take control of roads and clear what he described as "illegal checkpoints" from them.

"All armed forces units, military police have to cooperate with national police and local authorities to take measures to increase contol at checkpoints to prevent the movement of illegal weapons and forces into towns and the capital," General Keo Kimyan said in a radio broadcast.

The general, who is loyal to Hun Sen, also said all "illegal and anarchic checkpoints" had to be destroyed on roads, waterways and railways and searches would be made in various places for illegal weapons.

The call came as troops loyal to the country's rival prime ministers clashed on the outskirts of Phnom Penh after Hun Sen's men approached a military base under the control of troops loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Hun Sen repeated on Saturday his accusation that Ranariddh was bringing Khmer Rouge defectors into Phnom Penh illegally. Hun Sen said earlier he would use force against anyone found bringing "illegal troops" into the capital.
